findings.claim: The frozen-format test 'ignores the reserved action bit when decoding' still expects bit 2 to decode as nothing. To keep it passing, decodeInputs sets `action` as a non-enumerable property. Any spread, structuredClone or JSON.stringify of a decoded frame drops the action without a sound, which is a trap for the next night that copies or records replay inputs (for example B13 rival boosts).
findings.evidence: tests/sim/replay.test.ts:63-66 `it('ignores the reserved action bit when decoding', () => { const text = bytesToBase64(Uint8Array.from([0x00, 0b111])); expect(decodeInputs(text, 1, 1)).toEqual([[{ steer: 0, throttle: true, brake: true }]]); });`. Since B12, bit 2 is a live flag: src/sim/replay.ts:6 'bit2 action (fire the power-up…)' and :26 `const FLAG_ACTION = 4;`. The workaround is src/sim/replay.ts:96-98: `// Non-enumerable, so frames still deep-equal what pre-pickup decoders gave (bit 2 used to be ignored) while input.action reads true and stepWorld fires.` `if ((flags & FLAG_ACTION) !== 0) Object.defineProperty(input, 'action', { value: true, writable: true, configurable: true });`. It is the only defineProperty in src/. The behaviour is already pinned through the public value by tests/sim/pickup-replay.test.ts:21-34, which checks `decoded?.[0]?.action` is true and that 'action' is not in frames with bit 2 clear.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: change replay.test.ts:65 to expect `{ steer: 0, throttle: true, brake: true, action: true }` (or delete the case, since pickup-replay AC6 covers it). Then replace the defineProperty at replay.ts:96-98 with a plain `input.action = true` and drop the comment. stepWorld reads `input.action` the same way, so replays and bot laps don't change.

findings.claim: Ten browser test files each copy the same ~17-line beforeAll/afterAll harness: mkdtemp, a vite build of harness/screens, serve, launch Chromium, then close and rm. tests/ui/hud-motion.ts already exports exactly this as a generic `setup()`, but its name and comment tie it to B09, so the next browser-test night will make an eleventh copy. Every file, and each of the 8 hud-motion files, also runs its own full vite build: about 18 builds per `pnpm test`.
findings.evidence: tests/ui/keycap-style.test.ts:27-38 `beforeAll(async () => { dist = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'keycap-style-')); await build({ configFile: 'harness/screens/vite.config.ts', logLevel: 'silent', build: { outDir: dist, emptyOutDir: true } }); ({ origin, server } = await serve(dist)); browser = await launch(); }, 120_000); afterAll(async () => { await browser?.close(); server?.close(); rmSync(dist, { recursive: true, force: true }); });`, and the same in tests/ui/track-card-press.test.ts:33-44. The identical build call appears at results-fit-phone:24, keycap-legend-resize:32, desktop-start-screen:63, desktop-hud-scale:42, countdown-clear-browser:39, keycap-legend-slide:55, desktop-hud:72 and best-lap-e2e:284. The shared copy is tests/ui/hud-motion.ts:42-65 `export function setup(): { browser(): Browser; origin(): string }` (same body, with prefix 'hud-motion-'), used only by the 8 hud-motion-*.test.ts files.
findings.suggestedFix: A night may add a new tests/ui/browser-build.ts (or tests/browser.ts) exporting hud-motion's `setup()` under a neutral name, so new browser tests import it instead of copying. Owner: point hud-motion.ts and the ten files at it and delete their local beforeAll/afterAll blocks. A vitest globalSetup that builds once would also remove the ~18 repeated builds, but the vitest config is owner-only.
